title: Quasi-coherent graded direct-image algebras from homogeneous section products
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $T$ a scheme over $S$ [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism over $S$ that is quasi-compact and separated [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. Regard $T$ as its representable algebraic space [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Use the small etale module direct image and tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $(B_d)_{d\geq0}$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], with $\mathcal O_X$-bilinear homogeneous products $B_m\otimes B_n\to B_{m+n}$ and a unit $\mathcal O_X\to B_0$, compatible with restrictions and satisfying associativity, ordinary commutativity, and the unit laws. Tensor products mean sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; the total graded object is the coproduct in module sheaves, not an assertion that sections on every open commute with infinite coproducts. For each $d$, restriction of $f_*B_d$ to Zariski opens is a quasi-coherent Zariski module $A_d$, and its associated small etale module is canonically $f_*B_d$, with the comparison identity on sections of opens [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. There is a canonical commutative unital graded structure on the family $(A_d)$ [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]: on an open $V\subseteq T$, its product is the product of compatible sections of $B_m$ and $B_n$ over $X\times_TV$; its unit is pullback of regular functions followed by the unit of $B_0$. The sheaf coproduct $A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}A_d$ with these products is a quasi-coherent Zariski algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra], and its associated etale module is canonically $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}f_*B_d$, respecting every summand and homogeneous product. In particular these conclusions apply to $B_d=L^{\otimes d}$ for any line module $L$ on $X$, with $B_0=\mathcal O_X$ and the canonical tensor-power products; every such $B_d$ is quasi-coherent and the tensor-power products satisfy the stated graded algebra laws.

source.place: Tag 0D3C (lemma-descending-property-ample), proof: section-algebra paragraph; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03M9 (lemma-pushforward) and preceding representable-pushforward discussion, applied degreewise.

proof.text: Put $C_d=f_*B_d$. The quasi-coherent pushforward theorem applies to each $B_d$: its source is an algebraic space, its target is the scheme $T$ regarded as an algebraic space, and its required quasi-compactness and separatedness are hypotheses. Hence $C_d$ is quasi-coherent on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. The Zariski--etale equivalence now gives the quasi-coherent Zariski module $A_d(V)=C_d(V\hookrightarrow T)$ and its canonical comparison $E(A_d)\simeq C_d$, where $E=\epsilon_T^*$. The equivalence explicitly identifies this comparison on open-subscheme sections with the identity.

source.place: Tag 03M9, lemma-pushforward; descent.tex Tag 03DX, proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent (small etale equivalence).

proof.text: Construct the products before restricting to opens. For an etale test scheme $V\to T$, use the chart-limit description of $C_d(V)$. If $s\in C_m(V)$ and $t\in C_n(V)$, define $st$ by its projection at each chart $(U,a)$ over $X$ and $V$: $\pi_{U,a}(st)=\mu_{m,n}(\pi_{U,a}s\otimes\pi_{U,a}t)$. The right sides form a compatible family because every chart restriction commutes with $\mu$. For $r\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, scalar multiplication on that chart is through $a^\sharp$, so bilinearity of $\mu$ gives $(rs)t=r(st)=s(rt)$. The chart family $a^\sharp(r)\,1_{B_0|U}$ similarly defines the unit map $\mathcal O_T\to C_0$. These formulas commute with maps of $V$, since the chart projections defining direct image do. Thus they define bilinear sheaf products and a linear sheaf unit; the tensor and sheafification universal properties turn the bilinear products into maps $C_m\otimes C_n\to C_{m+n}$.

source.place: Tag 03M8, lemma-compute-pushforward, proof; sites-modules.tex Section 03EK, section-tensor-product.

proof.text: Every chart projection sends $(st)u$ and $s(tu)$ to equal sections by associativity of the given products on $B$; it sends $st$ and $ts$ to equal sections by ordinary commutativity, and $1s,s1$ to $s$ by the unit laws. Equality in the defining limit is equality of all projections, so the laws hold for $C_d$. Restrict these operations to open subschemes of $T$. They make $(A_d)$ a commutative unital graded sheaf algebra in the specified sense. For an open $V$, the displayed product is exactly the product of compatible sections over $X\times_TV$, and the unit formula is pullback of regular functions followed by the given unit. These are sheaf products; no sectionwise commutation with an infinite sum is involved.

source.place: Tag 0D3C, lemma-descending-property-ample, section-algebra paragraph; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03M8, chart-section description.

proof.text: Form the categorical module-sheaf coproduct $A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}A_d$. Extend the homogeneous products by the direct-sum and sheafification construction in the definition of graded sheaf structures. Explicitly, on the presheaf direct sum use the finite convolution $(xy)_k=\sum_{m+n=k}x_my_n$; finite support makes this defined, and restrictions preserve it. Bilinearity and sheafification extend it to the sheaf coproduct, with the degree-zero unit. Associativity is the equality of the two finite sums indexed by $i+j+k=d$; commutativity swaps $m,n$; the unit law has only the degree-zero term. These identities extend by the same universal properties. The coproduct-closure theorem applies to the small indexing set $\mathbb N$ and the quasi-coherent $A_d$, so $A$ is quasi-coherent as a module and therefore as an algebra.

source.place: Section 01LA, section-quasi-coherent, item (3); sites-modules.tex Section 03EK; spaces-descent.tex Tag 0D3C, section-algebra paragraph.

proof.text: The association functor $E$ is tensor pullback along $\epsilon_T$, by the Zariski--etale equivalence. The ringed-topos module adjunction makes it a left adjoint. Apply preservation of colimits to the discrete small category $\mathbb N$: $E(A)$ is the coproduct of the $E(A_d)$. Composing the inverse of that canonical coproduct comparison with the degreewise comparisons of Step 1 gives $\alpha:E(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_d C_d$. By construction, $\alpha\circ E(\iota_d)$ is the $d$th inclusion composed with $E(A_d)\simeq C_d$, so it respects each specified summand.

source.place: Tag 06VE, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits, item (2); sites-modules.tex Tag 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; categories.tex Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact (1).

proof.text: Use the canonical tensor-pullback comparison to view the associated homogeneous product as a map $E(A_m)\otimes E(A_n)\to E(A_{m+n})$. On local tensor generators its comparison is $(b\otimes s)\otimes(c\otimes t)\mapsto bc\otimes(s\otimes t)$. Under the degreewise counits $q_d:E(A_d)\simeq C_d$, the generator $b\otimes s$ maps to $b\,s|_U$ on an etale chart $U\to T$, since $E\dashv\epsilon_{T,*}$ is the tensor adjunction and $\epsilon_{T,*}C_d=A_d$. Consequently both compared products send this pair to $bc\,(st)|_U$, using the restriction formula of Step 2; the unit comparison sends $b\otimes r$ to $b\,r|_U\,1$. Tensor products and pullbacks are sheafifications of these locally generated tensors, so the universal properties extend these equalities uniquely. The same equalities on each pair of summands prove that $\alpha$ respects all homogeneous products and the unit.

source.place: Tag 06VE, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits (7); sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, and Tag 03D7, tensor adjunction proof.

proof.text: Finally suppose $L$ is a line module. On a trivializing etale chart choose a frame $e$. Define $B_0=\mathcal O_X$ and $B_d=L^{\otimes d}$ for $d>0$. The same chart identifies $B_d$ with $\mathcal O_X$ by $e^{\otimes d}$, including the empty tensor $1$ at $d=0$. Hence $B_d$ has there the presentation $0\to\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}B_d\to0$, and is quasi-coherent by the site-local presentation definition. Canonical tensor-power multiplication sends $(a e^{\otimes m})\otimes(b e^{\otimes n})$ to $ab e^{\otimes(m+n)}$. Associativity, ordinary commutativity and the unit laws are thus the ring identities $(ab)c=a(bc)$, $ab=ba$ and $1a=a1=a$. A change of frame $e\mapsto u e$ multiplies both sides by $u^{m+n}$, so these formulas are the canonical products and agree on overlaps; in degree zero $u^0=1$. The sheaf axiom gives the identities globally. Steps 1--6 therefore apply.
